Supply interruption and compensation policy (Marrowfield district). Tessmoor Water: Supply interruption and compensation policy (Marrowfield district). Version 1, effective 2026-01-15. Owner: Customer Experience.
This policy covers planned and unplanned interruptions to supply in the Marrowfield district, and what customers receive when an interruption runs long.

Customers receive at least 48 hours notice of a planned interruption.

Planned work is published on the website and on the district notice board. Vulnerable customers on the priority register get a phone call as well.

If an unplanned outage lasts longer than 12 hours, each affected household is credited $40.

Meter reading and estimated billing rules (Sorrelton district). Tessmoor Water: Meter reading and estimated billing rules (Sorrelton district). Version 2, effective 2026-01-15. Owner: Metering. This version replaces version 1.
These rules set how often meters in the Sorrelton district are read and when an estimated bill may be sent instead of a reading.

Meters are read every 3 months.

Readers carry a handheld device that checks each reading against the customer's usual use and asks for a photo when the reading looks unusual.

No more than 3 estimated bills in a row may be sent to the same customer.

Complaints handling procedure. Tessmoor Water: Complaints handling procedure. Version 1, effective 2026-01-15. Owner: Customer Experience.

Every complaint is acknowledged within 2 working days.

Leak response standard (Quillby district). Tessmoor Water: Leak response standard (Quillby district). Version 1, effective 2026-01-15. Owner: Network Operations.
This standard sets how quickly Tessmoor Water responds to reported leaks in the Quillby district and how response crews are staffed. A priority-one leak is a burst main, or any leak that cuts supply to more than fifty properties. All other visible leaks are priority-two.

Crews must be on site within 3 hours of a priority-one leak report.

Response times are measured from the moment the report is logged, not from dispatch. Weather warnings do not pause the clock, but the controller records any access problems on the job.

For a priority-two leak, the attendance target is 8 hours from the report.

Leak reports arrive through the contact centre, the online form and the field team. The duty controller logs each report, checks for duplicates nearby and assigns a priority before dispatch.

Each priority-one job is staffed by at least 6 field technicians.

After the repair, the crew reinstates the surface or books a reinstatement visit, photographs the site and closes the job with the cause of the leak.

Supply interruption and compensation policy (Marrowfield district). Tessmoor Water: Supply interruption and compensation policy (Marrowfield district). Version 1, effective 2026-01-15. Owner: Customer Experience.
This policy covers planned and unplanned interruptions to supply in the Marrowfield district, and what customers receive when an interruption runs long.

Customers receive at least 48 hours notice of a planned interruption.

Planned work is published on the website and on the district notice board. Vulnerable customers on the priority register get a phone call as well.

If an unplanned outage lasts longer than 12 hours, each affected household is credited $40.

During long interruptions bottled water is delivered to priority-register customers first, then made available at a collection point.

Credits are applied to the next bill automatically; customers do not need to claim them.

Billing and late payment policy (Marrowfield district). Tessmoor Water: Billing and late payment policy (Marrowfield district). Version 1, effective 2026-01-15. Owner: Customer Billing.
This policy explains how Tessmoor Water handles unpaid bills for household customers in the Marrowfield district, including fees and payment plans for customers who fall behind.

A late payment fee of 4% of the overdue balance is added after the grace period.

Before any fee is applied the account team sends a reminder by the customer's preferred channel. Customers who tell us they are struggling are offered a call with the support team.

Customers have 14 days after the due date before the account is treated as overdue.

Fees are never added to accounts that are in a registered dispute, and they are refunded if the bill turns out to be wrong.

A payment plan can spread arrears over at most 9 months.

Bills are issued after each meter reading. Customers can pay by direct debit, card, bank transfer or at a partner counter, and can change their payment date once a year.

Before any fee is applied the account team sends a reminder by the customer's preferred channel. Customers who tell us they are struggling are offered a call with the support team.

Customers have 14 days after the due date before the account is treated as overdue.

Fees are never added to accounts that are in a registered dispute, and they are refunded if the bill turns out to be wrong.

A payment plan can spread arrears over at most 9 months.

Bills are issued after each meter reading. Customers can pay by direct debit, card, bank transfer or at a partner counter, and can change their payment date once a year.

New service connection procedure (Marrowfield district). Tessmoor Water: New service connection procedure (Marrowfield district). Version 1, effective 2026-01-15. Owner: Developer Services.
This procedure covers new domestic water connections in the Marrowfield district, from quote to the first reading of the new meter.

The standard fee for a new domestic connection is $480.

Quotes are valid for ninety days. If the site changes after the quote, the applicant must ask for a new survey.

Connections are completed within 25 business days of a paid quote.

Applicants submit a site plan and the expected number of occupants. A surveyor checks the nearest main, the pressure and any road permits before a quote is issued.

The connection is finished when the meter is fitted, flushed and the first reading is recorded.

This standard sets how quickly Tessmoor Water responds to reported leaks in the Quillby district and how response crews are staffed. A priority-one leak is a burst main, or any leak that cuts supply to more than fifty properties. All other visible leaks are priority-two.

Crews must be on site within 3 hours of a priority-one leak report.

Response times are measured from the moment the report is logged, not from dispatch. Weather warnings do not pause the clock, but the controller records any access problems on the job.

For a priority-two leak, the attendance target is 8 hours from the report.

Leak reports arrive through the contact centre, the online form and the field team. The duty controller logs each report, checks for duplicates nearby and assigns a priority before dispatch.

Each priority-one job is staffed by at least 6 field technicians.

After the repair, the crew reinstates the surface or books a reinstatement visit, photographs the site and closes the job with the cause of the leak.

This standard sets how quickly Tessmoor Water responds to reported leaks in the Quillby district and how response crews are staffed. A priority-one leak is a burst main, or any leak that cuts supply to more than fifty properties. All other visible leaks are priority-two.

Crews must be on site within 3 hours of a priority-one leak report.

Response times are measured from the moment the report is logged, not from dispatch. Weather warnings do not pause the clock, but the controller records any access problems on the job.

For a priority-two leak, the attendance target is 8 hours from the report.

Leak reports arrive through the contact centre, the online form and the field team. The duty controller logs each report, checks for duplicates nearby and assigns a priority before dispatch.

Each priority-one job is staffed by at least 6 field technicians.

After the repair, the crew reinstates the surface or books a reinstatement visit, photographs the site and closes the job with the cause of the leak.

Q: What does the billing and late payment policy say for Sorrelton? A: A payment plan can spread arrears over at most 9 months.

Q: What does the new service connection procedure say for Sorrelton? A: Connections are completed within 15 business days of a paid quote.

Customers have 21 days after the due date before the account is treated as overdue.

Fees are never added to accounts that are in a registered dispute, and they are refunded if the bill turns out to be wrong.

Billing and late payment policy (Quillby district). Tessmoor Water: Billing and late payment policy (Quillby district). Version 1, effective 2026-01-15. Owner: Customer Billing.
Customers have 7 days after the due date before the account is treated as overdue.

Bills are issued after each meter reading. Customers can pay by direct debit, card, bank transfer or at a partner counter, and can change their payment date once a year.

A payment plan can spread arrears over at most 24 months.

Supply interruption and compensation policy (Quillby district). Tessmoor Water: Supply interruption and compensation policy (Quillby district). Version 1, effective 2024-04-01. Owner: Customer Experience.
This policy covers planned and unplanned interruptions to supply in the Quillby district, and what customers receive when an interruption runs long.

Customers receive at least 72 hours notice of a planned interruption.

Credits are applied to the next bill automatically; customers do not need to claim them.

If an unplanned outage lasts longer than 12 hours, each affected household is credited $40.
